candidates.name: Fort Saint-Jean
candidates.content: Fort Saint-Jean is a fortification at the North-Western end of the Old Port, built in 1660 by Louis XIV. The fort also hosts the Museum "Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée", but the fortification itself is a

candidates.name: Museum of the Decorative Arts, Fashion and Ceramics
candidates.alt: Musée des Arts décoratifs, de la Faïence et de la Mode
candidates.content: Château Borély and its grounds are pretty impressive before you start with the museum. Often the exhibits are scattered amongst the furniture in the house.

candidates.name: Vieux Port
candidates.content: Watching fishermen selling their stock by auction is a must. Arriving into Marseille in the Vieux-Port on a summer evening is something you will never forget. You can watch this show by going to Frioul islands or Chateau d'If and

candidates.name: Basilique Notre Dame de la Garde
candidates.content: The big church which overlooks the city. Old fishermen used to have their boats blessed in this church. You can still see many boat models hanging around in the church. From there it is one of the nicest view of the city. You can

candidates.name: Le Panier
candidates.content: Le Panier (which means basket in French) is the historical centre of the city. This district is characterized by many narrow and steep streets. The tourist office organises a guided tour in English of the Old town every Saturday a

candidates.name: Place Jean Jaurès
candidates.content: La Plaine is the local name for Place Jean Jaurès close to Cours Julien. Every Thursday and Saturday morning the Plaine market is the place to shop. If you are there early enough you can make very good deals, even if what you'll f

candidates.name: Palais Longchamp
candidates.content: It houses the city's Musée des Beaux-Arts and Natural History Museum. The surrounding park (the Parc Longchamp) is listed by the French Ministry of Culture as one of the Notable Gardens of France. The Boulevard Longchamp connects

candidates.name: Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée
candidates.content: The first French national museum outside of Paris. It has large permanent and temporary exhibitions. Its architecture mixes a very contemporary structure (a dark box) with an old castle, with footbridges linking the two parts of t

candidates.name: Museum of Contemporary Art [MAC]
candidates.content: Later works from the Cantini collection. Situated in southern suburbs but easily reached by Metro then bus. Now reopened after a major refurbishment.

candidates.name: Musée des Docks Romains
candidates.content: Built to preserve the archeological finds at the former warehouses of the old harbour from Phoenician and Roman times. (closed summer 23 check before going)

candidates.name: Archaeological Museum
candidates.content: Displays of Egyptian antiquities and classical antiquities.

candidates.name: Marseille History Museum (MHM)
candidates.price: Permanent collections: free; Exhibitions circa €6, reduced €3
candidates.content: Discover 26 centuries of history in archaeology, fine arts, everyday objects & architecture. There is a mobile app.

candidates.name: Marseille Cathedral
candidates.alt: Cathédrale Sainte-Marie-Majeure de Marseille or Cathédrale de la Major
candidates.content: A Byzantine-Roman cathedral at the western side of Le Panier quarter.

candidates.name: La Vieille Charité
candidates.content: is a wonderful old monument, a former charitable housing for poor, now hosting museums and exhibitions.

candidates.name: Musée Cantini
candidates.content: Museum focusing on modern art from the late 19th century until the mid-late 20th century.

candidates.name: Place Castellane
candidates.content: With a grand fountain/column/sculpture in the center, with excellent cinemas and cafés surrounding. There is another place called La Castellane: it is a poor suburb of Marseille where famous footballer Zinedine Zidane was born.

candidates.name: Parc Borély
candidates.content: A large and great park containing Château Borély, 300 meters from the sea. After a siesta in the park go have a drink at Escale Borely (a place with numerous restaurants and bars on the beach) to see the sunset.

candidates.name: Motorcycle Museum
candidates.price: Permanent collection: free, exhibitions eur6-12 also free for -18 & EU students 18-26
candidates.content: Museum in a former flour mill featuring motorcycles from 1885 to the present day. Four levels of bikes. It may look closed but you need to press the button by the gate to gain admission.

candidates.name: L'Hotel de Ville
candidates.content: Marseille City Hall

candidates.name: Cours Julien
candidates.content: A hangout area with bookstores, cafés, fountains, and a playground for the small ones. It is a trendy area of Marseille.

candidates.name: Noailles quarter
candidates.content: Lined with Arabic and Indo-Chinese shops some of the streets could be part of a bazzaar in Algeria. A fascinating area.

candidates.name: Vallon des Auffes
candidates.content: Small and out of time traditional fishing port, just near the city centre.

candidates.name: Musée des beaux-arts de Marseille
candidates.content: The painting collection includes works of the French, Italian, Spanish and Northern (Flanders and Holland) schools.

candidates.name: FRAC Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur
candidates.content: Contemporary art in a building designed by architect Kengo Kuma. Part of a national network .

candidates.name: Deportation Memorial
candidates.content: Memorial & museum relating to repression & persecution during World War II. Run by the Marseille History Museum (MHM).

candidates.name: CEPAC Silo
candidates.content: Concert venue/theatre in a former grain silo. The performance space is reconfigurable according to the type of show performed. Total capacity 2,050 seats.

candidates.name: Artplexe
candidates.content: New multi-screen cinema showing some films in VO combined with exhibition spaces and restaurant.

candidates.name: City of Music
candidates.content: Music school & concert halls Diverse musical types

candidates.name: Cinéma l'Alhambra
candidates.content: Art House Cinema with original 1930s facade out of the city centre. Shows some films in VO (the original language)

candidates.name: Le Trolleybus
candidates.content: This three room cave-like club, is a great place to go if you like to listen to different types of music. One room or cave, plays hit music, another room plays underground techno and house music (room led by La Dame Noir records),

candidates.name: Le Cosy Bar
candidates.content: Le Cosy Bar is a club aimed at the younger demographic. This is a multi-roomed club, plays top music in techno, dub step, hip hop, and reggae til 06:00. Le Cosy Bar is known for their extravagant theme nights such as Moscow Beach,

candidates.name: Le Palais de la Major
candidates.content: Restaurant and club under the Major cathedral, the place hosts live bands from Corsica playing French and international hits. The place is luxurious and beautiful people fit in.

candidates.name: Red Lion cours Julian
candidates.content: Small pub

candidates.name: Red Lion
candidates.content: English pub at La Pointe Rouge, southern Marseille, next to the beach.

candidates.name: Beer District Marseille
candidates.content: Beer Hall

candidates.name: Les BerThoM Marseille
candidates.content: Modern craft beer bar.

candidates.name: La Cane bière
candidates.content: Enormous selection for such a small place. Confusingly not on the Canebière.

candidates.name: La Brasserie Communale
candidates.content: Microbrewery serving locally brewed beers

candidates.name: Bière Academy
candidates.content: Craft beer bar a few streets away from the old port.

candidates.name: Polikarpov
candidates.content: Lively and good value late bar with outside terrace. Does a wide range of cocktails and one of the cheaper places for beer.

candidates.name: Le Petit Nice Passédat
candidates.content: A 3-star Michelin restaurant on an idyllic location by the sea, facing the islands, held by local celebrity chef Gérald Passédat. It ranks among Southern France's very best restaurants and serves the best bouillabaisse in town at

candidates.name: Brasserie Le Saint Victor
candidates.content: A very friendly neighborhood brasserie with good traditional dishes and caring, fast and efficient staff. The catering is excellent with a wide variety of daily specials.

candidates.name: Four des Navettes
candidates.content: This bakery is famous for its "Navette" dry biscuit which recipe has been kept secret for almost a century. This is one of Marseille's culinary specialities. Not to miss, through you can get it in other bakeries in Marseille, too.

candidates.name: Le Cercle Rouge
candidates.content: This unusual restaurant does excellent Corsican tapas such as figatelli sausage, stuffed artichokes, panchetta in honey and red mullet in tomato sauce. Worth booking to get a spot on the lovely terrace.

candidates.name: Café Cantine
candidates.content: This little place has the best food made fresh onsite! Very kind and friendly staff. Fast service, fresh and good products. Very warm welcome and very good homemade meal.

candidates.name: Moon Burger
candidates.content: The quality is exceptional, the products are fresh, the bread is homemade, the meat is succulent. The homemade sauces are top of the line. Also the staff is very warm and attentive.

candidates.name: five pizza original
candidates.content: Interesting concept, which is very simple: You create your pizza by choosing all the toppings of your pizza with a lot of choice on an electronic terminal.

candidates.name: Café l'Écomotive
candidates.content: Excellent veggie café

candidates.name: 1860 Le Palais
candidates.content: Very good classic French cuisine, made from quality products, in the historic building of the Chamber of Commerce. One of the best places near the old port.

candidates.name: Sampolo
candidates.content: Sampolo is a nice family place. The dishes and desserts are very tasty and homemade. Great place and great atmosphere in the evening.

candidates.name: Santa Pizza
candidates.content: Very good pizza and pasta. Hearty toppings, thin crust, tasty ingredients.

candidates.name: Perle d'Asie
candidates.content: A cuisine that makes us rediscover Asian flavors. There is a possibility of having vegetarian spring rolls.

december.text: You can visit the fabulous restaurants and cafes. You can go and do many adventurous things such as diving and hiring boats! The calanques (fjords) between Marseille and La Ciotat are a very popular sports climbing area. And of course, if the weather is fine, you can simply go to the beach!

La Foire aux Santons is a very picturesque Christmas market held from late November near the Canebière and Vieux Port. Provence is the home of santons, terracotta figurines used in nativity scènes known as crèches. Some merchants and many churches display impressive crèches of their own.
